legal_items.prompt: A projectile has vertical velocity 12 m/s upward at t = 1 s. Take g = 10 m/s^2. What was its initial vertical velocity?
hint_texts: Keep one clock from launch to the stated event.
Think about how gravity changes the vertical velocity each second.

legal_items.prompt: During a projectile flight the vertical component is 6 m/s upward at t = 2 s. With upward positive and g = 9 m/s^2, determine the launch vertical component.
hint_texts: Use the same vertical-motion relationship you used in the direct example.

legal_items.prompt: A v_y-versus-time graph is a straight line through (0 s, 24 m/s) and (2 s, 6 m/s). State the vertical acceleration and launch vertical velocity.
hint_texts: Read the starting vertical velocity directly from the graph.
What physical quantity does the slope of a velocity-time graph represent?

legal_items.prompt: A projectile is launched with vertical component 30 m/s. Its vertical component later becomes 3 m/s upward. If the vertical acceleration is -9 m/s^2, find how long after launch this state occurs.
hint_texts: What quantity is unknown this time?
The physical model has not changed; only the target has changed.
